h: The Added Letters That Guard Yosef Pinchas and Yisrael

p: בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג ריג, ב)
In the holy Zohar on this parshah (III 213b):
'He set it as a testimony in Yehosef,' etc.
as one who did not know her language;
'And she caught him by his garment,' etc.
וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ צָוַח לָקֳבְלֵיהּ (מִשְׁלֵי ז, ה)
And the holy spirit cried out before him (Mishlei 7:5):
'To guard you from the strange woman,
from the foreign woman who makes her words smooth.'
The hei that was added to him,
as it is written, 'a testimony in Yehosef.'
a yud was added to Pinchas,
because he was zealous in this."
the whole connection of the opening to this parshah
that just as a hei was added to Yosef,
so a yud was added to Pinchas;
and it would have sufficed to bring the pasuk
that a hei was added to him,
why does it need the whole exposition?
And if it is to bring proof
that the letter hei is testimony,
"The tribes of Yah, a testimony for Yisrael":
that the letters hei and yud were added,
to testify that they are the sons of their fathers.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
according to what is written in the holy Zohar
in the opening of Rabbi Yehudah (Tehillim 86:2):
that there is no letter in the Torah
that does not have in it
וְיַקִּירִין מְרַמֵּז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And "precious" alludes to the Oral Torah,
according to what is written in the Midrash
וְכָל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ (אִיּוֹב כח, י)
"'And his eye saw every precious thing' (Iyov 28:10):
this is Rabbi Akiva and his companions."
"And by knowledge the rooms are filled
with all precious and pleasant wealth";
and in Rashi's commentary, Ki Sisa (Shemos 31:3):
"'And with knowledge': this is the holy spirit."
the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
so that a halachah l'Moshe mi'Sinai is stated in accordance with him;
"A sage is greater than a prophet."
And Malchus is the holy spirit,
which we call Torah she'b'al peh";
and it is the spirit from that holiness above,
is alluded to in the Written Torah;
"Is there anything written in the Kesuvim
that is not alluded to in the Torah?"
and so too the entire Oral Torah;
and this is "the spirit from that holiness above."
And this is what the holy Zohar says,
that in every letter of the Torah
there are secrets of the Written Torah.
And likewise the renewal of words of Torah
כָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ אוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה
each one has a letter in the Torah
and this is his portion in the Oral Torah;
יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
has a portion in the Oral Torah,
"An inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov";
"It is not written 'the congregation of Yannai,'
that is, even the am ha'aretz,
who are called "the house of Yaakov"
and says: "And this hei guards it";
go out to receive and guard it,
into the dwelling of its place!"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רב, רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א)
to break the yetzer hara except Torah."
And "to bring it into the dwelling of its place"
שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
which is also through words of Torah,
a cure for what came before.
וְעַל זֶה פָּתַח רַבִּי חִיָּיא אֲבַתְרֵיהּ
And on this Rabbi Chiya opened after him:
"He set it as a testimony in Yehosef,"
where there is also an extra hei.
And it says that at first
as one who did not recognize her language;
yet in truth he did recognize her language,
did not enter his heart at all
and had no effect on him whatsoever,
until it is written, "And she caught him by his garment";
some slight hold for a moment,
until he was forced to flee outside.
And similarly it is also expounded in the Midrash
"And the arms of his hands were made supple":
that his bow was weakened, etc.
"A language that I did not know":
that he made himself as one who did not recognize her language,
וְכָל פִּתּוּיֵי לֹא נִכְנַס כְּלָל לְלִבּוֹ
and all her enticements did not enter his heart at all;
שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ בּוֹ אֵיזֶה תְּפִיסָה לְשָׁעָה
that she had some hold on him for a moment,
and was forced to flee outside;
and were it not for the Holy One, blessed is He, helping him,
And this is what it says:
that the holy spirit cried out before him,
"To guard you from the strange woman, etc.,
that she smoothed the matter for him,
in that she caught him by his garment,
that is, that she had a connection to him;
"Just as this one acted for the sake of Heaven, etc.:
that she was destined to raise a son from him,
וְלֹא יָדְעָה אִם מִמֶּנָּה אִם מִבִּתָּהּ
and did not know whether from herself or from her daughter."
And in this pasuk there are
חֲמִשָּׁה תֵּיבוֹת עִם ה׳ בְּסוֹף הַתֵּיבָה
five words with a hei at the end of the word:
for so too, on the opposite side, in the kelipah,
the serpent, the wife of harlotry,
goes after the woman of valor,
like an ape that goes after a person,
כְּמוֹ דְּאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קמח, ב)
and this is the aspect of Malchus of the kelipah.
that from her would come Mashiach ben Yosef,
as indeed he came from her daughter,
but she made darkness into light.
And this is why there is in two words,
which indicates also the lower yud,
which is the secret of the covenant;
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן הָיָה לָהּ בּוֹ
and thereby she had on him
a slight hold for a moment;
only that the holy spirit cried out before him,
"To guard you from the strange woman,"
And he, on his part, strove
of the eve of Shabbos, which
"is fear, and fear dwells in her"
and the upper hei guards him;
and this is "He set it as a testimony in Yehosef."
which is fear, the aspect of the lower hei,
and the yetzer hara clears out from there;
"And the Children of Yisrael shall keep the Shabbos,
(as is written in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48).
And this is "a testimony in Yehosef":
"testimony" indicates that it is for all eternity.
"The tribes of Yah, a testimony for Yisrael":
yud-hei alludes to Chochmah and Binah,
and this is a testimony for Yisrael for all eternity;
"It is a tradition that a tribe will not be wiped out";
for the holiness of each tribe
and this is a testimony for all eternity;
and similar to what is written
in the preceding opening of Rabbi Yehudah:
וְהַיְינוּ כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה לג, טז)
That is, similar to what is said (Yeshayahu 33:16),
meaning that it is for all eternity;
and this is indicated by there being a yud
which indicates that it reaches the root,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
along the lines of what is written (Zohar II 175b):
through being zealous for the covenant,
had the letter yud added to him,
that is, that it be his and his descendants'
and as is written in the holy Zohar above:
"And this tzaddik is called a chassid."
